principles.text: Design deep modules: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface. Apply the deletion test: if deleting a module makes its complexity vanish, it was a pass-through; if the complexity reappears across its callers, it earns its keep.
principles.rationale: From codebase-design: depth gives callers leverage and maintainers locality.

principles.text: Put a seam only where something actually varies: one adapter is a hypothetical seam, two adapters are a real one.
principles.rationale: From codebase-design: a speculative seam adds interface without adding leverage.

principles.text: Accept dependencies instead of constructing them, and return results instead of producing side effects, so the interface is also the test surface.
Work in vertical slices: one failing test at an agreed seam, the least code that makes it pass, then the next. Red before green; refactor in review, not inside the loop.
principles.rationale: From tdd: tests written in bulk ahead of the code verify imagined behaviour.

principles.text: Mock only at system boundaries (external services, time, randomness), never your own modules, and take expected values from an independent source, not by recomputing them the way the code does.
principles.rationale: From tdd: implementation-coupled and tautological tests break on refactors and never disagree with the code.

principles.text: Before forming a theory about a bug, build a tight feedback loop: one fast, deterministic command that goes red on the reported symptom. No loop, no hypothesis.
principles.rationale: From diagnosing-bugs: with a loop that goes red on this bug, bisection and hypothesis testing become mechanical.

principles.text: Rank several falsifiable hypotheses before testing any, each stating the prediction it makes, and change one variable per probe.
principles.rationale: From diagnosing-bugs: a single hypothesis anchors on the first plausible idea.

principles.text: Lock a fix with a regression test written before the fix, at the seam where the bug actually occurs; when no such seam exists, record that as an architectural finding instead of writing a shallow test.
principles.rationale: From diagnosing-bugs: a test at the wrong seam gives false confidence.

principles.text: Review a change on two separate axes: does it follow the documented standards, and does it do what the spec asked. Report them apart so one cannot mask the other.
principles.rationale: From code-review: correct code can implement the wrong thing, and the right thing can break the conventions.

principles.text: Keep one glossary of the domain's terms and use them exactly in code, tests and docs; when a term conflicts with the glossary or the code, resolve it and record the result.
principles.rationale: From domain-modeling: a shared vocabulary names the seams and keeps humans and agents talking about the same thing.

principles.text: Record a decision as an ADR only when it is hard to reverse, surprising without context and the result of a real trade-off.
principles.rationale: From domain-modeling: a decision record that meets all three stops the next reader re-litigating it.

principles.text: Answer a design question with a throwaway prototype, marked as one and kept off the main branch; carry only the validated decision into the real code.
principles.rationale: From prototype: the prototype exists to learn fast, not to ship.

principles.text: Write agent-facing docs as ordered steps that end on checkable completion criteria; keep each meaning in one place and state the behaviour you want, not the one you forbid.
principles.rationale: From writing-for-agents: vague criteria invite premature completion, and duplication and negation add variance.
